name: Duck 2.1
summary: Duck 2 plus a stride stance start, trained from zero
what_changed: Same recipe as Duck 2, except the start of each attempt: after the usual random nudge, a coin flip picks the leading leg and one hip swing starts 0.04 rad forward and the other 0.04 rad back (each twice the random nudge, so the nudge can never close the gap).
why: Duck 2 without its wobble fell in the first second in 34 of 60 starts. A check showed why: from a near mirror image pose the symmetric brain sends mirror image leg commands and dives forward, and a perfectly even pose always fell. On Duck 2's best brain, untrained for it, the stride start cut early falls to 2 of 60 and walked 30 of 30 attempts at 0.4 m/s. Keeping the wobble instead was rejected: it doubles the energy per metre (38 against 18 J). A point version because the change is small.
starts_from: zero (same seed and untrained brain as Duck 1 and Duck 2)

runs.outcome: Like Duck 2 up to 1.25M (all exams fall), then 212 at 1.5M and 916 with 0 falls at 1.75M, where Duck 2 had 460. From there it held between 828 and 986 with at most 2 falls, ending on its best, 986 with 0 falls at 4.0M. No collapse. The step size fell to about 0.00002 by the end

notes: Walks every start of the exam and 10 of 10 walking test attempts, at 12.3 J per metre (Duck 2: 15 to 18). The exam ceiling at its efficiency is about 980 to 1,000, so on flat ground it is close to the most our scoring can tell. It still walks a little faster than asked (7.5 m per exam attempt where the asked speeds give 6.3 m). Duck 3 starts from this brain. Challenges (speed, backpack, perilous road of tall stones, rocks): see challenges/README.md.

world_settings.notes: Duck 1, Duck 2 and Duck 2.1. They trained under an older forward reward, without the overshoot rule (going faster than asked did not lose points); this world has today's rule.
